scope.quote:
In testing whether economies of scale exist for tax planning, I first perform
empirical tests on a broad sample of U.S. domestic and multinational corporations.
I then focus the analysis on a subsample of U.S. multinational corporations only.
I estimate the following ordinary least squares (OLS) regression using a broad sample of firms to test Hypotheses 1, 2, and 3:

I use two different proxies for foreign operations in the empirical tests. I use the MNC dummy variable in (1) to determine whether multinational firms have lower or higher ETRs than other firms. I use the ratio of foreign assets to total worldwide assets, FOROPER, in (2) below to determine whether firms with more extensive foreign operations have lower or higher ETRs than other firms:
While MNC tests whether systematic differences exist between the ETRs of multinational and domestic-only companies, FOROPER tests whether economies of scale exist for foreign tax planning.

Table 5 presents
results of regressions of worldwide ETRs on test and control variables, for a sample
of multinational corporations only. In particular, Table 5 presents estimated coefficients for (3) and (4). I perform these regressions to determine whether the relations between ETRs and the extent of foreign operations in a sample of multinational corporations only are different from the broader sample of firms.

Table 6 presents results of regressions of U.S. and foreign ETRs on test and
control variables for the sample of multinational corporations only. In particular,
Table 6 presents estimated coefficients for (5) and (6). I perform these regressions
to determine whether the relations between ETRs and test variables differ between
the U.S. and foreign tax jurisdictions.

method.quote: This table presents the results of OLS regressions

WWETR = α 0 + α 1 SIZE +α 2 PTI +α 3 FOROPER + α 4 FOROPER <sup>2</sup> +α 5 MNC + α 6 MNCxSIZE +α 7 MNCxPTI +α 8–19 LOCATION +α 20–25 INDUS
+α 26–32 YEAR + ε (2)

review_notes: Table 4 reports 16,750 firm-year observations for equation (2), while the ETR sample-selection section reports 19,737 observations available for ETR analysis. The paper does not explain the lower equation-specific count; its exact reported fit N is retained without inferring the cause.

The supplied reading text renders greater-than signs in the Table 1 MNC rule and multiplication signs in the interaction definitions as hyphens. The original physical PDF page 11 was visually inspected and shows FORPTI > 0, FOROPER > 0, MNC × PTI, and MNC × SIZE; the literal reading-text quotations are retained.

results_review_notes: The selected baseline is Table 4 column (2), equation (2), the broad-sample worldwide ETR regression. Column (1), multinational-only tables, and other equations are excluded.

The printed Table 4 includes seven frozen predictors, an intercept and twelve LOCATION fixed-effect coefficients. Its note explicitly says the INDUS and YEAR coefficients are not tabulated; no estimates are inferred for them.
Table 4 reports t-statistics but no standard-error estimator, degrees of freedom, or complete one-tailed direction. The threshold legend is preserved without inferring exact p-values.
